name: Global STEM Leadership Scholarship
subject: Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence
fundingDetails: Full tuition coverage, $24,000 annual living stipend, health insurance, and $2,000 conference travel stipend.
eligibility: Open to international students worldwide including South Asian candidates
Undergraduate degree in STEM with minimum GPA of 3.6 / 4.0
Demonstrated research interest or open-source software contributions
Proof of English proficiency (TOEFL 95+ or IELTS 7.0+)
requiredDocuments: Official academic transcripts
Statement of Purpose (Research goals & societal impact)
3 Letters of Recommendation
Curriculum Vitae / Resume
Portfolio of relevant projects or publications
applicationInstructions: Complete the online application form on the provider portal, upload verified academic credentials, and submit research proposal before the deadline.

name: Nepal Himalayan Tech & Innovation Bursary
subject: Information Technology, Software Engineering, Electronics
fundingDetails: 100% tuition waiver for 4-year undergraduate degree plus laptop subsidy of NPR 60,000 for top 5 recipients.
eligibility: Citizens of Nepal with completed +2 Science or Diploma in Engineering
Minimum 3.2 GPA in high school board examinations (NEB)
Household income criteria for need-based consideration
Commitment to 1 year of community digital literacy initiative
requiredDocuments: NEB Character and Mark Certificates
Citizenship certificate (Nagarikta) or parent verification
Income recommendation from local Ward office
500-word personal essay on 'How Technology Can Transform Rural Nepal'
applicationInstructions: Submit application through the central university scholarship portal along with certified ward documents and statement of purpose.

name: Commonwealth Sustainability Excellence Award
subject: Environmental Science, Climate Resilience, Public Policy
fundingDetails: Approved airfare to and from the UK, approved tuition fees, living stipend of £1,347 per month, and thesis grant.
eligibility: Citizen of or permanent resident in an eligible Commonwealth country
Hold a first degree of at least upper second class (2:1) honours standard
Unable to afford to study in the UK without this scholarship
Development impact proposal aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals
requiredDocuments: Proof of citizenship or refugee status
Full academic transcripts and university certificates
Development Impact Statement (4 sections)
Two signed references uploaded directly by referees
applicationInstructions: Apply via the CSC Electronic Application System (EAS) and ensure supporting referees submit before the portal closes.

name: DAAD Clean Energy Research Grant
subject: Renewable Energy, Green Hydrogen, Electrical Engineering
fundingDetails: Monthly stipend of €1,200, health and accident insurance, travel subsidy, and €460 annual research allowance.
eligibility: Bachelor's or Master's degree completed within the last 6 years
Demonstrated research proposal with a hosting German university advisor
Working knowledge of English (B2/C1) or German (TestDaF level 4)
Strong academic record with published papers prioritized
requiredDocuments: Detailed research proposal (maximum 10 pages)
Written confirmation from academic host/supervisor in Germany
Complete CV in Europass format
Certified copies of all higher education diplomas and grade sheets
applicationInstructions: Register on the DAAD online portal, upload all German/English sworn translations, and submit to the regional DAAD information center.

name: Asia-Pacific Digital Frontiers Fellowship
subject: Cybersecurity, Distributed Systems, Blockchain, Fintech
fundingDetails: Full tuition, SGD 8,000 annual living allowance, one-time computer grant of SGD 2,000, and guaranteed internship placement.
eligibility: Open to international citizens residing in Asia-Pacific region
Outstanding academic achievements in mathematics and computing
Participation in national science olympiads or programming contests is an asset
Strong leadership and co-curricular extracurricular profile
requiredDocuments: High school graduation certificates & standardized test scores
Coding portfolio link (GitHub/GitLab)
Two letters of recommendation from math or computer science teachers
Personal reflection essay on ethical decentralized systems
applicationInstructions: Submit directly to participating universities (NUS, NTU, SMU) and select the Asia-Pacific Digital Frontiers Fellowship checkbox.

name: Erasmus Mundus Decentralized Web & Data Masters
provider: European Education and Culture Executive Agency
subject: Distributed Computing, Web3 Technologies, Cryptography
fundingDetails: €1,400 per month for up to 24 months, full tuition waiver across three partner universities, visa and travel costs covered.
eligibility: Hold a recognized first degree in computer science, mathematics, or related field
Must study in at least two different European countries during the programme
Fluent in English (CEFR C1 level or equivalent IELTS 7.0)
Global applicants eligible regardless of country of origin
requiredDocuments: Certified English translation of bachelor degree & transcripts
Motivation letter explaining track preference and career vision
Curriculum vitae highlighting technical projects and open-source work
Passport scan and two reference contact forms
applicationInstructions: Apply through the consortium website during the open call. Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an online interview in February.

name: Global Women in Tech & Engineering Fellowship
subject: Software Engineering, Robotics, Biomedical Engineering
fundingDetails: CAD $15,000 per academic year renewable for 4 years, mentorship pairing with senior female industry leaders, and annual summit pass.
eligibility: Female-identifying students admitted to an accredited Canadian university engineering program
Minimum 85% high school average or equivalent 3.5+ GPA
Demonstrated passion for mentorship or promoting diversity in STEM
International applicants warmly welcomed
requiredDocuments: High school transcripts and proof of Canadian university conditional offer
Video submission (2 minutes) introducing your engineering passion project
One reference letter from a teacher, community mentor, or employer
Financial need summary statement (optional)
applicationInstructions: Upload your application and unlisted YouTube/Vimeo video link to the Ada Lovelace Foundation student dashboard.

name: Nordic Clean Energy Sustainability Tuition Award
subject: Renewable Systems, Smart Grids, Circular Economy
fundingDetails: 100% tuition fee waiver for the entire 2-year master's programme. Recipients also gain access to the Nordic Alumni Network for Sustainability.
eligibility: Citizens of designated DAC-listed countries (including Nepal, Bangladesh, Vietnam)
Minimum 3,000 hours of demonstrated work experience, research, or volunteer leadership
Admitted to an eligible Swedish master's programme via Universityadmissions.se
Commitment to return to home country or region to implement sustainability initiatives
requiredDocuments: Swedish Institute specific CV template
Proof of work and leadership experience forms (official stamps required)
Two letters of reference on official templates
Valid passport copy
applicationInstructions: First apply to Swedish universities via the national portal, then apply for the SI scholarship using your application number.

name: Australian Research Discovery Scholarship (RTP)
subject: Applied Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing, Bio-informatics
fundingDetails: AUD $34,500 annual tax-free stipend for up to 3.5 years, full tuition fee offset, overseas student health cover (OSHC), and relocation allowance.
eligibility: Domestic and international postgraduate researchers
First Class Honours degree, Master by Research, or equivalent demonstrated research track record
Endorsement by an accredited principal research supervisor in Australia
English language proficiency requirements met
requiredDocuments: Research proposal (2,000 words) with methodology and expected outcomes
Academic curriculum vitae detailing peer-reviewed conference or journal papers
Complete certified transcripts and degree testamurs
Two academic referee reports
applicationInstructions: Apply concurrently with your PhD candidature application at the participating Australian university graduate research school.

name: South Asian Young Changemakers Grassroots Grant
subject: Social Sciences, Public Health, Environmental Policy
fundingDetails: $5,000 annual educational grant, seed funding of $2,500 for a local community initiative, and regional exchange summit participation.
eligibility: Youth aged 17–25 currently enrolled or accepted into an undergraduate programme in South Asia
Active track record in local community service, youth leadership, or environmental action
Demonstrated financial need or first-generation university student status
Commitment to report on community project milestones every 6 months
requiredDocuments: Proof of university enrollment or acceptance letter
Community project pitch (1 page) explaining the local challenge addressed
One recommendation letter from a local NGO, teacher, or community leader
Short personal bio and photo
applicationInstructions: Complete the online application form and attach your community impact proposal and recommendation letter.
